authors: Lund H, Werner S, Wiltshire R, et al.
title: 4th Generation District Heating (4GDH): Integrating smart thermal grids into future sustainable energy systems
what_it_supports: Defines the 4th generation district heating concept as part of future sustainable (low-carbon) energy systems; Crossref title is the short form '4th Generation District Heating (4GDH)' and no abstract is available via Crossref/OpenAlex.

authors: Lund H, Ostergaard PA, Nielsen TB, Werner S, et al.
title: Perspectives on fourth and fifth generation district heating
what_it_supports: Abstract: 4GDH describes a transition path for decarbonisation of the DH sector (defined in detail in 2014), and 5GDHC shares the overarching decarbonisation aim.

title: International review of district heating and cooling
what_it_supports: Abstract: reviews the global/European position of DH and notes low recognition of possible CO2 emission reductions from district heating.

title: Achieving low return temperatures from district heating substations
what_it_supports: Abstract: low supply and return temperatures are important for efficient DH, low return temperatures require substations and secondary systems without temperature faults, and 4GDH will require lower distribution temperatures.

title: Fault detection in district heating substations
what_it_supports: Abstract: DH temperature levels are still too high; eliminating substation and customer-system faults could reduce them considerably; threshold methods on hourly meter data found faults in 74% of 135 Swedish substations.

authors: Mansson S, Johansson Kallioniemi PO, Thern M, Van Oevelen T, Sernhed K
title: Faults in district heating customer installations and ways to approach them: Experiences from Swedish utilities
what_it_supports: Title-level only (no abstract retrievable): reports Swedish utilities' experience with faults in DH customer installations and how they are handled.

title: Economic benefits of fourth generation district heating
what_it_supports: Abstract: lower distribution temperatures lower heat supply costs (strongly for geothermal, excess heat and heat pumps), and high distribution temperatures are a barrier to renewable/recycled heat.

authors: Neumayer M, Stecher D, Grimm S, et al.
title: Fault and anomaly detection in district heating substations: A survey on methodology and data sets
what_it_supports: Abstract: early detection of substation faults is crucial for DH efficiency and 4GDH low temperatures; most published work is unsupervised anomaly detection because labelled data sets are lacking.

authors: Wang J, Yang F, Chen T, Shah SL
title: An overview of industrial alarm systems: Main causes for alarm overloading, research status, and open problems
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering 13(2):1045-1061
what_it_supports: Abstract: most industrial alarm systems produce too many alarms for operators (alarm overloading); identifies chattering alarms, misconfigured alarm variables, isolated alarm design and abnormality propagation as main causes.

authors: Beebe D, Ferrer S, Logerot D
title: The connection of peak alarm rates to plant incidents and what you can do to minimize
what_it_supports: Abstract: many plants still struggle to control alarm floods; discusses safety, environmental and economic justification for alarm management.

authors: Izadi I, Shah SL, Shook DS, Kondaveeti SR, Chen T
title: A framework for optimal design of alarm systems
what_it_supports: Title-level only (no abstract retrievable): framework for optimal alarm-system design (supports citing formal alarm design as a trade-off problem).

title: ANSI/ISA-18.2-2016 Management of Alarm Systems for the Process Industries
venue: International Society of Automation (ISA), Research Triangle Park NC
what_it_supports: UNVERIFIED (standard, no DOI; edition/year from general knowledge, not checked against a public record): alarm-management lifecycle standard.

title: EEMUA Publication 191: Alarm systems - a guide to design, management and procurement (3rd edition)
venue: Engineering Equipment and Materials Users' Association, London
what_it_supports: UNVERIFIED (no DOI; 3rd edition/2013 from general knowledge; Crossref only confirms a 2nd edition launch notice in 2007, doi:10.1177/002029400704000805): industry guideline on alarm-system design and management.

title: Assessment of control loop performance
venue: The Canadian Journal of Chemical Engineering 67(5):856-861
what_it_supports: Abstract: the minimum-variance best achievable control can be estimated by fitting a univariate time series to routine closed-loop operating data (the basis of the Harris index).

title: An overview of control performance assessment technology and industrial applications
what_it_supports: Title-level only (no abstract retrievable): overview of control performance assessment methods and their industrial applications.

title: Advances and new directions in plant-wide disturbance detection and diagnosis
what_it_supports: Title-level only (no abstract retrievable): review of plant-wide disturbance (e.g. oscillation) detection and diagnosis in process control.

title: Control performance monitoring - a review and assessment
what_it_supports: Title-level only (no abstract retrievable): review and assessment of control performance monitoring methods.

title: Using SCADA data for wind turbine condition monitoring - a review
what_it_supports: Abstract: reviews SCADA-based condition monitoring of wind turbines and categorises approaches including normal behaviour modelling, trending, clustering and alarm assessment.

authors: Liu FT, Ting KM, Zhou ZH
title: Isolation Forest
venue: Proc. 8th IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM 2008), pp. 413-422
what_it_supports: Abstract: proposes iForest, which isolates anomalies rather than profiling normal points, with linear time complexity and low memory.

authors: Ke G, Meng Q, Finley T, et al.
title: LightGBM: A highly efficient gradient boosting decision tree
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
what_it_supports: Verified via OpenAlex W2768348081 (no DOI): introduces LightGBM, an efficient gradient boosting decision tree implementation.

title: Regression quantiles
what_it_supports: Title-level (no abstract retrievable): introduces regression quantiles (linear quantile regression), the basis for quantile-based normal bands.

title: Greedy function approximation: A gradient boosting machine
what_it_supports: Abstract: develops gradient boosting for arbitrary fitting criteria including least absolute deviation (median) loss, with regression-tree base learners (TreeBoost).

authors: Hermans S, Al Koussa J, Van Oevelen T, Vanhoudt D
title: Fault detection for district heating substations: Beyond three-sigma approaches
what_it_supports: Abstract: replaces a Gaussian three-sigma error model with a quantile regression model for time-conditioned fault thresholds in DH substations (also listed under need 8).

title: Current time series anomaly detection benchmarks are flawed and are creating the illusion of progress
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (early access 2021; Crossref record has no volume/pages)
what_it_supports: Abstract: most exemplars in popular TSAD benchmarks suffer from four flaws, so many published comparisons may be unreliable and apparent progress illusory.

authors: Kim S, Choi K, Choi HS, Lee B, Yoon S
title: Towards a rigorous evaluation of time-series anomaly detection
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 36(7):7194-7201
what_it_supports: Abstract: the point-adjustment protocol can heavily overestimate detection performance (even random scores look state-of-the-art), leading to misguided rankings.

title: Evaluating real-time anomaly detection algorithms - the Numenta Anomaly Benchmark
venue: Proc. IEEE 14th Int. Conf. on Machine Learning and Applications (ICMLA), pp. 38-44
what_it_supports: Abstract: proposes NAB for streaming detectors; the ideal detector detects anomalies early, triggers no false alarms and adapts to changing statistics.

authors: Tatbul N, Lee TJ, Zdonik S, Alam M, Gottschlich J
title: Precision and recall for time series
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 31 (NeurIPS 2018), pp. 1920-1930
what_it_supports: Abstract: many real-world anomalies are range-based, so point-based precision/recall are extended to ranges.

authors: Guck C, Roelofs CMA, Faulstich S
title: CARE to compare: A real-world benchmark dataset for early fault detection in wind turbine data
what_it_supports: Abstract: publishes a labelled wind-turbine SCADA dataset (36 turbines, 3 farms, 44 labelled time frames) for comparing early fault detection algorithms (and proposes an evaluation score; check full text for the CARE score definition).

title: Individual comparisons by ranking methods
what_it_supports: Original signed-rank / rank-sum test paper (title-level).

title: Note on the sampling error of the difference between correlated proportions or percentages
what_it_supports: Abstract: formulas for testing the difference between correlated (paired) proportions; basis of McNemar's test.

title: A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure
doi: no DOI (JSTOR 4615733; 10.2307/4615733 listed by OpenAlex but not registered)
what_it_supports: Abstract: sequentially rejective multiple test procedure controlling family-wise type I error for any combination of true hypotheses.

title: Bootstrap methods: Another look at the jackknife
what_it_supports: Abstract: introduces the bootstrap for estimating the sampling distribution of a statistic from observed data.

title: An Introduction to the Bootstrap
venue: Springer US (Crossref record of the book)
what_it_supports: Standard textbook reference for bootstrap confidence intervals (title-level).

title: Bootstrapping clustered data
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 69(3):369-390
what_it_supports: Abstract: analyses bootstraps for clustered (one-way) data and shows consistency of variance estimates depends on the modelling of the clustering.

authors: Cameron AC, Gelbach JB, Miller DL
title: Bootstrap-based improvements for inference with clustered errors
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics 90(3):414-427
what_it_supports: Abstract: standard cluster-robust tests over-reject with few (5-30) clusters; cluster bootstrap-t procedures restore nominal size.

title: Statistical comparisons of classifiers over multiple data sets
what_it_supports: Abstract: recommends Wilcoxon signed-rank test for two classifiers and Friedman test with post-hoc tests for multiple classifiers over multiple data sets.

authors: Hermans S, Al Koussa J, Van Oevelen T, Vanhoudt D
title: Fault detection for district heating substations: Beyond three-sigma approaches
what_it_supports: Abstract: in field DH substation data, baseline-model errors are not i.i.d. Gaussian but show clear seasonality over time, and training the baseline is complicated by this time dependency.

title: Sensor fault detection and diagnosis of air-handling units using a condition-based adaptive statistical method
what_it_supports: Abstract: PCA models for AHU FDD must be updated to follow normal process shifts due to changing (outdoor) working conditions; a condition-based adaptive scheme improves detectability over a time-based one.

title: Change-point detection in wind turbine SCADA data for robust condition monitoring with normal behaviour models
what_it_supports: Abstract: change points from malfunctions/maintenance violate the clean-training assumption of normal behaviour models; about one-third of 600 SCADA signals over 2 years were affected.

authors: Gama J, Zliobaite I, Bifet A, Pechenizkiy M, Bouchachia A
title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
what_it_supports: Abstract: defines concept drift (changing input-target relation over time) and surveys adaptive learning strategies and their evaluation.
